Top N values index

topn.Rd

topn returns the indices (or values) of the n largest or smallest values in a vector. This extends which.max and which.min, which return only the first such index.

The resulting order is the same as order(vec, decreasing = decreasing, na.last = TRUE)[1:n] when hasna is TRUE or vec has no missing values, but topn() avoids sorting the whole input. It is therefore much faster when n is small relative to the input size.

Usage

topn(vec, n=6L, decreasing=TRUE, hasna=TRUE, index=TRUE)

Arguments

vec

A numeric or integer vector. Other types are not supported yet.

n

A positive integer greater than or equal to 1.

decreasing

Logical. If TRUE (default), sort from largest to smallest. This is the same as decreasing in base::order, whose default is FALSE.

hasna

Logical. Whether vec contains NA values. Default is TRUE.

index

Logical. If TRUE (default), return indices. If FALSE, return values.

Details

For small n, topn() uses memory proportional to n. It falls back to base::order() when n > 1500 and hasna = TRUE, or when n > 2000 and hasna = FALSE. It also falls back when the selection scan has to rescan too often, for example when vec is already sorted in the opposite direction. The fallback allocates a full-length index: about 4 bytes per element. This can use much more memory than the fast path.

For inputs longer than .Machine$integer.max, topn() keeps a heap of at most n entries instead, so memory stays proportional to n (about 24 bytes per entry plus 8 bytes per returned index). Class attributes are ignored and the stored values are compared. Unlike base::order(), decreasing = TRUE works for these inputs. For n above roughly three quarters of the input length this heap can use more memory than a full-length order() index, and order() is faster for decreasing = FALSE.

For classed numeric vectors shorter than .Machine$integer.max, xtfrm() is applied once before selection, so their order matches order()/xtfrm().

Value

If index = TRUE, an integer vector of the indices of the n largest (or smallest) values in vec. If index = FALSE, the values themselves. For inputs longer than .Machine$integer.max, the indices are returned as a double vector.

Ties keep their input order. With hasna = TRUE (default), missing values are placed last, in input order. hasna = FALSE asserts that vec has no missing values: it is not checked, and for unclassed vectors NA is then compared as an ordinary value. For inputs longer than .Machine$integer.max, missing values are always placed last, whatever the value of hasna. For inputs no longer than .Machine$integer.max, the resulting order matches order(vec, decreasing = decreasing, method = "radix", na.last = TRUE)[1:n] when vec has no missing values or hasna = TRUE.

Author

Morgan Jacob

Examples

x = rnorm(1e4)

# Example 1: index of top 6 negative values
topn(x, 6L, decreasing=FALSE)
#> [1] 3859 9372 5250 9081 4216 7502
order(x)[1:6]
#> [1] 3859 9372 5250 9081 4216 7502

# Example 2: index of top 6 positive values
topn(x, 6L, decreasing = TRUE)
#> [1] 9437 3328 4002 8436 6252 1202
order(x, decreasing=TRUE)[1:6]
#> [1] 9437 3328 4002 8436 6252 1202

# Example 3: top 6 negative values
topn(x, 6L, decreasing=FALSE, index=FALSE)
#> [1] -3.304182 -3.165100 -3.153828 -3.112280 -3.004550 -2.998378
sort(x)[1:6]
#> [1] -3.304182 -3.165100 -3.153828 -3.112280 -3.004550 -2.998378

# Benchmarks
# ----------
# x = rnorm(1e7) # 76Mb
# microbenchmark::microbenchmark(
#   topn=kit::topn(x, 6L),
#   order=order(x, decreasing=TRUE)[1:6],
#   times=10L
# )
# Unit: milliseconds
#  expr min   lq  mean median   uq  max neval
# topn   11   11    13     11   12   18    10
# order 563  565   587    566  602  661    10
#
# microbenchmark::microbenchmark(
#  topn=kit::topn(x, 6L, decreasing=FALSE, index=FALSE),
#  sort=sort(x, partial=1:6)[1:6],
#  times=10L
# )
# Unit: milliseconds
# expr min  lq  mean median   uq  max neval
# topn  11  11    11     11   12   12    10
# sort 167 175   197    178  205  303    10
